# Motivation

## Nature is invisible in the accounts

- Ecosystems supply services the economy depends on, from pollination and soil retention to coastal protection and carbon storage, yet none of them appear in standard national accounts.
- Unmeasured, the loss of these services surfaces only later — as lower yields, higher damages and higher prices.
- The Gross Ecosystem Product (GEP) account values what ecosystems supply, country by country and service by service, so natural capital can be tracked alongside GDP.
- The same service models also drive scenario analysis: how climate and land-use scenarios change the services economies depend on, feeding the macroeconomic pipelines.

## Why one reviewed library

- Different GEP service models were developed by different contributors in different repositories, with their own layout, path conventions and aggregation choices.
- The library brings them into one repository with one layout: every service runs the same way, reproduces its numbers on rerun, and writes the same per-country table the GEP account reads.
- A GEP account changes decisions only if every number can be traced to the model that produced it; the totals table carries each service's verification status.
- Central banks and finance ministries are asked to price nature risk, and the scenarios they use carry no ecosystem-service feedback; the pipeline this library feeds adds one.

# What global_invest is

## One module per service: GEP always, a shock where the science allows

- The library holds one folder per ecosystem service, all on the same file convention.
- Every one of the {{< meta n_services >}} services now carries its GEP method in the library; recreation still awaits its input data.
- Services whose science supports it also produce a scenario shock for the macroeconomic pipeline; not all can be made into shocks.
- A service with both outputs computes them from the same functions file — one implementation, so the valuation and the shock cannot disagree.
- The library is scenario agnostic. Consumers inject their naming through scenario maps and required configuration.

## The mental model: a service module reads like a paper

| File | In paper terms |
|---|---|
| functions.py | The equations — pure science; knows nothing about folders or projects. |
| tasks.py | The estimation steps — each caches its output and skips itself when already done. |
| initialize.py | The table of contents, plus the plug other pipelines graft in. |
| run_\<service\>.py | The main script — opens a workspace and goes. Thin on purpose. |
| method.qmd | The methods section — rendered from the code, so it cannot silently drift. |

- The three CSVs are the calibration tables. es_config says what each model reads and how it prices; es_scenarios says which scenarios and maps; es_parameters holds tuning knobs and machine locations.
- One rule ties data to code: a CSV cell is a default, and whatever the caller already set wins.

## The template every service follows

- One runner per task tree, and every run file shares one anatomy, applied across the library: build_task_tree names the pipeline, and the run is configured where it is constructed.
- Configuration is data, in two shared CSVs. es_config.csv holds one row per service in the GEP formula's own vocabulary (quantity, price, attribution, land base, base year, price convention) plus the crosswalk to the status sheet; es_scenarios_test.csv holds the standard SEALS scenarios and ships the matching test maps, so a standalone shock run works on any machine.
- The library fills only what the caller left unset. A pipeline such as ngfs_pnas drives the same tasks from its own scenarios file, and its values always win.
- Each task's first line publishes the inputs it needs (relative to the shared base data; each machine finds its own copy), so any task grafted anywhere is a working piece — rolling out service by service, terrestrial first.
- Aggregation is on r250, one row per country. The r264 crosswalk is used only for maps.

## How a run finds its data

- Every input is a reference path relative to the shared base data, and each machine resolves it for itself: the project's own input folder first, then the machine's base_data, then the cloud fallback.
- A run therefore carries no absolute paths. The same run file works on a laptop, on the cluster, or on any machine that stages the same base data — the recreation port and the landslide cluster run rely on exactly this.
- Tasks cache their output in the project directory and skip themselves when it already exists, so reruns are cheap and interrupted runs resume where they stopped.

## Two consumers, one science

- Each service module feeds two consumers from the same functions file: the GEP account reads the valuation (one row per country), and the macroeconomic pipeline reads the scenario shock (a table of productivity deviations for GTAP).
- Because both outputs are written from the same science, the account's value and the scenario's shock cannot drift apart — there is no second implementation to diverge.
- Not every service's science supports a shock, but every service is expected to reach a GEP valuation.

## How a pipeline grafts a service

- A consumer pipeline calls add_\<service\>_tasks(p) after its land-use step, and the service's tasks slot into the consumer's own task tree.
- Configuration is a defaults layer. The library's CSVs fill only what the caller left unset, and a caller's value always wins — so ngfs_pnas drives the same tasks from its own scenarios file, and the library never needs to know its consumers' naming.
- The standalone runners use the same graft, so a service debugged in isolation behaves identically inside the pipeline.

## The configuration table itself (es_config.csv)

- One row per service; the columns are the GEP formula's roles — Q = quantity input, P = price input, λ = attribution input, land = the LULC base — plus the crosswalk to this group's status sheet. An empty cell means the role does not apply.

| service | sheet crosswalk | base year | price convention | Q | P | λ | land |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| terrestrial_carbon | global_climate_regulation / terrestrial | 2019 | rental scc r2% | carbon zones raster | prices xlsx | | esa 2019 |
| coastal_carbon | global_climate_regulation / coastal | 2019 | rental scc r2% | | prices xlsx | | |

## Verification discipline, and what it caught

- Run first, conform second, and verify every conform step against the cached run. An additive gate audits each branch against develop.
- Write-time invariants check every shock table before it is written, a canonical-row rule guards every country aggregation, and every row of the configuration table is under test from the moment it is added.
- Caught so far: a 23.5 percent double-count in the carbon GEP, a two-spelling baseline bug, and a stale-input trap in the erosion chaining.
- It also caught one claim of our own: the coastal report's numbers are the EEZ-only aggregation by design, matched exactly by our run.
- Every receipt names its anchor, because the two kinds prove different things. Reproducing our own cached run proves a change moved nothing (every refactor is held to that, to the dollar); an external anchor — the manuscript, an author's replication — proves the number itself. The totals table names which kind each service has.
- Replication proves our code reproduces the reported results, not that the results are right. Most questions exist because verification found exactly where a decision, a source, or an input is missing.

## The test behind each service

| Service | Test module | What it pins |
|---|---|---|
| terrestrial_carbon | test_terrestrial_carbon.py | raster math on tiny synthetic GeoTIFFs; the static shock on a synthetic dependency table |
| coastal_carbon | test_coastal_carbon.py | the two aggregation contracts: only marine EEZ rows are valued, and the r250 collapse |
| pollination | test_pollination.py | end-to-end on a tiny value raster through real zonal statistics; a split country sums once |
| erosion | test_erosion.py | the valuation arithmetic itself (loaders mocked): elasticity shock, clipping, floor, GPV shares |
| recreation | test_recreation.py | every method constant against hand-derived values: matrices, ring kernels, gravity model, allocation |
| fire_protection | test_fire_protection.py | exact replication of the committed reference (161 countries) on every run, plus the reordered-input tripwire |
| fisheries | test_fisheries_headers.py + test_fisheries.py | header resolution and the HAR read-list union; the CWoN rent-trend math against hand-derived series |
| landslide_mitigation | — | run knobs pinned in the library tests; the science awaits the cluster run |
| the five accounting services | — | library-wide contract tests only (next line) |
| library-wide | test_es_config / parameters / scenarios / seams / utilities / r250_guard | every shipped CSV row hydrates, every shock seam stays grafted, the split-country guard stays present |

- The library-wide tests are the reason a NEW row or service is born under test: adding a row to a shipped CSV is automatically covered, and clobbering a service's entry point fails the seam test.
- Missing: science-level tests for the five accounting services and landslide — a small synthetic pin of each service's arithmetic, the way erosion and recreation have.

# The questions, service by service

## terrestrial_carbon: verified against the manuscript

- [State: GEP replicates the manuscript to the dollar, {{< meta terrestrial_total >}} at 2019. The strongest number in the library.]{.state}
- One correction to know about: a double-count in the CODE overstated its total by 23.5 percent (split countries entered once per sub-region — China six times). The published manuscript was right all along; the corrected aggregation reproduces it to the dollar, which is how the fix was validated.
- **No open questions.** This service is the template the others are held to.

## coastal_carbon: which side of the shoreline?

- [State: replicates the author's design exactly, mangrove component to the cent. One run, two totals: {{< meta coastal_eez >}} counting ocean-side rows only, {{< meta coastal_all >}} counting both sides.]{.state}
- **Q1 (design):** was EEZ-only chosen to avoid double-counting the land-side pixels with terrestrial carbon? The land side carries 97.5 percent of mangrove and 84 percent of salt marsh area, so the convention moves the total 4.5 times.
- **Q2 (inputs):** which exact seagrass and salt marsh input versions produced the report's {{< meta coastal_report >}}? Our replication gives {{< meta coastal_eez >}} with mangrove matching exactly, and the report's own seagrass area (62.21 Mha) exceeds the published range it cites (16 to 26.7 Mha).
- **Q3 (the room): If both sides should count, who owns the terrestrial-side mask that prevents double-counting?**

- [State: the service sheet lists Terrestrial, Coastal, and Marine carbon. We found no marine module in any repository and could not identify a lead — correct us if either exists.]{.state}
- **Q1:** is marine carbon in scope for the account at all, and on what horizon?
- **Q2:** if yes, who owns it, and which data product drives it?

## erosion: one science, two products, three methods

- One biophysical chain feeds everything: InVEST's SDR model yields actual soil loss (USLE) and bare-soil loss (RKLS); their difference is the erosion the land cover prevents.
- Two products come from it. The GEP valuation runs the chain once on observed land cover (prevention shares, on-farm and upstream, valued per country). The scenario shock reruns it per scenario and year on the SEALS maps.
- The shock has two paths: static reads the frozen dependency table (the default today); dynamic recomputes the full chain per map — expensive, and the reason the SDR steps cache themselves.
- Three shock methods are computed side by side and reported together: damage (thresholded area share), service (threshold-free, magnitude-weighted per crop), and service-threshold (service restricted to a fixed severe-pixel set) — the last is the default that becomes the GTAP shock, and one configuration row selects which.
- Two resolutions: a 6.45 km analysis grid that runs on a laptop, or native 300 m on a cluster — one configuration row switches them.
- The method's constants (the SES-11 thresholds) are named in code and await the author's blessing; every number from this service is provisional until then.

# Cross-cutting decisions

## Four conventions the room can settle today

- **Maps:** country values on split-country polygons render partially (China shows one sixth). We propose dissolving to one polygon per country, a one-time cartographic artifact that can never double-count. Any objection?
- **Base year:** {{< meta n_services_at_2019 >}} of {{< meta n_services >}} services value at 2019; pollination's raster is 2023 and gets regenerated after its definition is settled. Confirm 2019 as the account's base year.
- **Subsistence:** crop, livestock, and fisheries carry subsistence subgroups in the service sheet. In scope or not, per service?
- **The universe crosswalk:** the sheet lists roughly 26 services; the library covers ten. We propose a tested crosswalk table (sheet label to module to output) instead of restructuring modules to mirror the sheet. And the sheet's label typos should be fixed before anything inherits them.

## The August 31 write-up pass maps onto today

- Colleen's housekeeping email (due August 31) asks every group for consistent parameters and clean write-ups. Today's answers complete most of it a week early.
- **2019 dollars:** confirms our base year; pollination's regeneration will follow the sheet's deflator-conversion guidance once its definition is settled.
- **CWON rental rates, not GTAP:** renewable and fisheries already use CWON. For extractive, this is context for the 0.49 question — if that factor is a rental-rate choice, the CWON guidance may answer it.
- **EPA VSL:** landslide values mortality, so one open item — which VSL does v0.2.0 use?
- **Zeros vs NAs:** our verification hit exactly this — extractive has 9 countries NA for missing WB data (documented), and coastal_protection currently fills unmatched countries with zero in a merge, which needs the true-zero-or-NA review the email asks for. We will do that pass on our modules.
- **Discount rate 2 percent with 1 and 3 sensitivity:** the carbon services' rental SCC embeds a discounting choice — worth confirming it matches.

## One data fix and one naming fix

- Kosovo's row in the shared correspondence carries the country name "Serbia" with the correct label XKX. One cell corrected upstream makes every name-join and map legend right. Who owns the correspondence generation?
- The drive folder `gdp_inflation_delator` is missing an f. We staged under the corrected spelling; the drive folder should be renamed to match. Who owns submissions?

- **water_quality:** where the pipeline's code actually lives (the sheet's link doesn't contain it).
- **fire_protection:** the account's choice among the three GEP variants (the data asks are closed).
- **air_filtration:** where the code lives — the manuscript already carries its total, so one pointer to the pipeline makes it next into the library.
- **local_climate_regulation:** which entry point and script versions in the urban-cooling repo are canonical (several live side by side), and where its runs happen.
- **The room:** pollination's definition, the shoreline convention, crop's units, the map dissolve, base year 2019, subsistence scope, marine carbon's fate, the fisheries GEP's source.
- **Every service:** a complete SI-table row (status, value info, relationships to other services); leads for the unclaimed services; confirmation of the next-in-line for the library.

## What happens with the answers

- Every answer starts an already-scoped step, most of them mechanical: reference outputs trigger exact-replication verification (erosion, landslide, livestock), decisions trigger one-pass conversions (crop's units, the map dissolve), and the definitional calls trigger the regenerations that are already written up (pollination at 2019, the shoreline diagnostic).
- The questions live in a tracked document, and each closes with a verified number or a recorded decision.
- Each answer extends the same reproducibility to one more service. The goal for the next session like this one: no questions slide at all.
